This is a giant change so I put it through AI. It overall looks great but there are a few subtleties.
AI review Error: API error (attempt 1): UNAVAILABLE (code 503): The service is currently unavailable. (Error ID: 9404bd4c-562f-487e-a057-209b8930646f-148) Here is a review of **whatwg/html#13188** (*"Editorial: centralize HTML attribute change steps"*, `8a24596eafbb4631d1c73d892d643ca70944b753`). --- ### Summary Overall, this is a very clean and well-structured refactoring that: 1. Introduces a per-element **HTML element attribute change steps** hook (`#html-attribute-change-steps`) alongside the existing insertion, post-connection, removing, and moving hooks, and centralizes the shared attribute change steps (`nonce`, element-reference reflection, `form`, `accesskey`, `blocking`, `id`/`name` for `rel="expect"`, `popover`, and event handler content attributes) into `#html-attribute-change-steps`. 2. Consolidates scattered prose attribute-mutation triggers ("Whenever an element's `foo` attribute is set, changed, or removed...") into explicit **HTML element attribute change steps** for `a`/`area`, `source`, `img`, `iframe`, `audio`/`video`, `track`, `input`, `select`, `optgroup`, `option`, `details`, `dialog`, `script`, `canvas`, and `frame`. 3. Standardizes the ordering of element lifecycle hooks across the spec (`insertion` → `post-connection` → `removing` → `moving` → `attribute change`). Static analysis (`check_webidl.py` and `check_algorithms.py`) passes with no new Web IDL or algorithm defects. --- ### Findings #### 1. Ordering of internal-slot/reflection updates vs. per-element hooks in `#html-attribute-change-steps` (`source` lines 1931–1956) In `#html-attribute-change-steps`: ```html

  • If element's namespace is the HTML namespace, and this standard defines HTML element attribute change steps for element's local name, then run the corresponding HTML element attribute change steps given element, localName, oldValue, and value.

  • If localName is nonce and element includes HTMLOrSVGOrMathMLElement:

    1. If value is null, then set element's [[CryptographicNonce]] to the empty string.

    2. Otherwise, set element's [[CryptographicNonce]] to value.

  • If element has an explicitly set localName-element, then set it to null.

  • If element has explicitly set localName-elements, then set it to null.

    • ``` Just as the prose immediately above notes that `#html-attribute-change-steps` runs *after* DOM's attribute change steps that update `element`'s ID so that subsequent steps observe updated state, **Steps 3–5 (`[[CryptographicNonce]]` and clearing `explicitly set localName-element(s)`) should run *before* Step 2 (`HTML element attribute change steps`)**. While none of the current per-element `HTML element attribute change steps` read `[[CryptographicNonce]]` or `get the attr-associated element(s)` today, running the foundational internal-slot and reflection-cache updates before the element-specific hook ensures that any future per-element hook consolidated under `#10331` (for example, `commandfor`/`popovertarget` or script/style nonce handling) will not observe a stale `[[CryptographicNonce]]` or stale `explicitly set attr-element(s)`. --- #### 2. `XREF-CODE-VS-SPAN` markup issue on `blocking attribute` (`source` line 1966) Line 1966 writes: ```html

  • If localName is blocking, oldValue is not value, and element is render-blocking but is no longer potentially render-blocking, then unblock rendering on element.

    • ``` `blocking attribute` (`source` line 8667) is a *concept* (like `lazy loading attribute`), not an `element-attr` definition (`attr-link-blocking`, `attr-script-blocking`, and `attr-style-blocking` are the `element-attr` definitions, each stating *"The `blocking` attribute is a `blocking attribute`"*). Referencing `data-x="blocking attribute"` with `` instead of `` violates HTML house style (`XREF-CODE-VS-SPAN`). To preserve the cross-reference to `blocking attribute` while keeping `` for the attribute name, consider either: ```html

  • If element has a blocking attribute, localName is "blocking", oldValue is not value, and element is render-blocking but is no longer potentially render-blocking, then unblock rendering on element.

    • ``` (where *"has a `blocking attribute`"* means `element` is an element for which a `blocking attribute` is defined, or simply use `"blocking"` since only `link`, `script`, and `style` can ever be `render-blocking`). --- #### 3. Redundant creation-time `poster` trigger and detached antecedent for `video` (`source` lines 37408–37412 and 38383–38385) In `The video element` (`source` lines 37408–37412), the PR retains the creation half of the original sentence: ```html

    When a video element is created, if the resource specified by its poster attribute is to be used, then determine a video's poster frame given the element.

    ``` and moves the mutation half 1,000 lines down into `The HTML element attribute change steps for audio and video elements` (`source` lines 38383–38385): ```html

  • If element is a video element, localName is poster, and the specified resource is to be used, then determine a video's poster frame given element.

    • ``` Two issues here: 1. **Creation trigger is a no-op**: When a `video` element is created via DOM's *create an element* (including via the HTML parser's *create an element for a token*), its attribute list is initially empty; any `poster` attribute is appended after creation (or via `attribute change steps`). Running `determine a video's poster frame` when `poster` is absent only sets `poster lazy load resumption steps` to `null` (already its initial value) and returns at step 2 (*"If there is no `poster` content attribute, then return"*). Removing the creation-time trigger at lines 37408–37412 would match how other attributes in this PR are handled. 2. **Detached antecedent at line 38384**: In the original location (`source` line 37371), *"if the specified resource is to be used"* referred back to the preceding paragraph (*"The resource given by the `poster` attribute, the poster frame..."*). At line 37409 (where that paragraph still sits right above), the PR expanded it to *"if the resource specified by its `poster` attribute is to be used"*, whereas at line 38384 (far from the `poster` section) it kept *"and the specified resource is to be used"*. Line 38384 should use the expanded phrasing *"and the resource specified by `element`'s `poster` attribute is to be used"*. --- #### 4. Minor / Editorial Polish - **`
    ` fragmentation in the `option` section (`source` lines 58935–59071)**: Moving `The option HTML element attribute change steps` down after `The option HTML element moving steps` in Commit 3 required wrapping `The option HTML element attribute change steps` in its own `
    ...
    ` (`source` lines 59022–59071) because the `option` state and lifecycle hooks added earlier (`cached nearest ancestor select element`, `insertion`, `post-connection`, `removing`, and `moving` steps at lines 58935–59020) were left outside `
    `. Moving the opening `
    ` above line 58935 and merging the adjacent `w-nodev` blocks would avoid splitting the `w-nodev` wrapper and properly exclude all of `option`'s internal algorithms from the developer edition. - **`track` element `src` removal (`source` lines 42918–42934)**: In `The track HTML element attribute change steps`, step 7 updates `element`'s `track URL` only `If value is not null:`, whereas step 8 empties the cue list unconditionally when `localName` is `src`. This faithfully preserves the pre-existing spec behavior (where setting/changing `src` updated `track URL` at former line 38105, while setting/changing/removing `src` emptied cues at former line 43145) — which is right for an `Editorial:` PR, though worth noting on `#10331` if not already tracked (`track URL` remains set to the old URL when `src` is removed, unlike `img`/`iframe`). --- ### Verification Summary by Section | Area | `source` Lines | Status | |---|---|---| | `#html-attribute-change-steps` & `HTML element attribute change steps` | 1784–1787, 1920–2030 | See Findings 1 & 2 | | `nonce` (`[[CryptographicNonce]]`) | 1939–1950, 8312 | Preserves `HTMLOrSVGOrMathMLElement` check | | Reflected element-reference attributes (`explicitly set attr-element(s)`) | 1952–1956, 9325, 9494 | Exact | | `render-blocking` / `blocking` attribute | 1966–1969, 12536 | See Finding 2 | | `a` and `area` (`href`, `ping`, `rel`, `referrerpolicy`, `name`) | 1986–1999, 27380–27400 | Exact | | `source` (`src`, `srcset`, `type`, `sizes`, `media`, `width`, `height`) | 31274–31305 | Exact; also extracts `source` removing steps | | `img` (`srcset`, `sizes`, `src`, `crossorigin`, `referrerpolicy`, `loading`) | 31577–31622, 33215 | Exact | | `iframe` (`src`, `srcdoc`, `sandbox`, `allow`, `loading`) | 35743–35785, 36067–36085 | Exact | | `video` and `audio` (`src`, `poster`, `loading`) | 37408–37412, 38373–38422 | See Finding 3 | | `track` (`src`, `kind`, `label`, `srclang`, `default`) | 38105, 42860–42937 | Exact (see Minor note on `src` removal) | | `input` (`type`, `value`, `checked`, `disabled`, `name`, `readonly`, `multiple`, `size`, `list`) | 51637–51737, 52405, 54020–54440 | Exact; extracts `update an input element's type` | | `select` (`multiple`, `size`), `optgroup` (`disabled`), `option` (`disabled`, `label`, `selected`) | 58046–58062, 58711–58718, 59022–59071 | Exact (see Minor note on `w-nodev`) | | `details` (`name`, `open`) and `dialog` (`open`) | 65965–66010, 67093–67135 | Exact | | `script` (`src`, `type`, `nomodule`, `async`, `blocking`) | 68516–68557, 68649 | Exact | | `canvas` (`width`, `height`) | 70769–70843 | Exact | | `accesskey`, `popover`, event handlers, `frame` (`src`) | 88493–88538, 92821, 124900–124942, 156959–156970 | Exact |

> 1. Ordering of internal-slot/reflection updates vs. per-element hooks in `#html-attribute-change-steps` (`source` lines 1931–1956)

I'm happy do this (or have you/your agent push a commit that does it) but I'm somewhat hesitant because our policy so far has been to put the per-element hooks first. That's what insertion, removing, and moving do. Maybe internal-slot/reflection is special and deserves and exception, but I'd want that exception to be made consciously with a human in the loop.

Fixed

> track element src removal

Apparently this is an interop issue. I'll open a separate issue and leave this change as purely editorial.
